title: The Jataka
altTitles: The Jataka, or Stories of the Buddha's Former Births
dateDisplay: Verses c. 3rd century BCE; prose commentary c. 5th century CE
attributionNote: The Jātaka verses are anonymous and belong to the oldest strata of the Pali canon; the prose stories that frame them were composed later and are traditionally ascribed to Buddhaghosa's commentary. The collection as translated here is the work of the editors of the Cambridge edition, not of a single author.
description: The Jataka is the great storybook of Buddhism: 547 tales of the Buddha's former births, from the hare that offered itself to a hungry brahmin to the long Vessantara story of the prince who gave away everything he had. Each story is told as an occasion in the Buddha's life, followed by the verses it illustrates and an identification of the characters as earlier and later births. The collection preserves a vast range of Indian narrative — animal fables, farce, romance, legal puzzles and the Bodhisatta's gradual perfection of generosity, virtue and wisdom.
historicalContext: The Jātaka belongs to the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali canon; its verses are among the oldest Buddhist poetry, while the prose commentary was compiled in Sri Lanka and is traditionally attributed to Buddhaghosa (5th century CE). E. B. Cowell edited the six-volume English translation (1895–1907), with Robert Chalmers, W. H. D. Rouse, H. T. Francis and R. A. Neil translating the several volumes.
availabilityNote: Complete. All 547 stories in the six volumes of Cowell's edition are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one story per chapter, in the printed order of the collection from No. 1 to No. 547. The volumes' prefaces, contents lists and indexes of names are not part of the work; the stories themselves include the verses, the prose frame and the identification of the characters.
